Dial a number in, tap "+ another set" to bank it and start the next — a drop set or a ramp is still one box, just built one set at a time instead of typed as a comma list. Weight gets a "." to switch the wheel to tenths for plates that aren’t whole numbers; reps stays whole numbers only. The docked comma key is gone — there is nothing left for it to assist.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.07.002: Sets, reps and weight dial together now, in one sheet — tap any of the three and reps and weight come up as two wheels side by side, "+ another set" banking the pair at once. Sets dropped its own dial entirely; it is just how many pairs you have banked. A "⌫" undoes the last banked pair back onto the wheels, or — with nothing banked yet — clears the whole thing back to empty, the way backspacing a typed box to nothing always did.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.09.001: The mark stretches to its new spot now instead of rolling there — a direct move, longer along the way it is travelling and thinner across it, round again the instant it stops. No more spinning through whole turns to cover the distance.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.10.001: The stretch now blurs slightly as it moves and leaves a handful of fading afterimages behind it — a trail of itself, not a smear of colour, and it paints behind the live mark the whole way, never over its face.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.10.002: Back to just the stretch — the blur and the afterimages it left behind are gone. The mark shifts, stretches along the way, and arrives plain, the way it did two versions ago.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.11.001: Logging a planned session on the wheel gives you what you dialed. A plan of 4 sets of 8 used to open with three sets already banked, so the set you were dialing was the fourth — 3 reps at 100 came back as 8,8,8,3 and 20,20,20,100. It now opens on one set, starting at the plan’s numbers, and + adds the rest. Opening the wheel and closing it without touching anything also no longer changes a thing.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.11.002: New versions arrive on their own now. Come back to the app after an update has shipped and it reloads straight into it — unless something is open or you are mid-entry, in which case you get the banner as before. It also checks every five minutes instead of every thirty.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.11.003: Nothing you can see — a note in the code about how long the mark takes to move now says 560ms, which is what it actually does.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.11.004: Did Upper on a Lower day? Log what you did and the app notices from the lifts: it records the session as Upper, and the next planned Upper in the coming week becomes the Lower you skipped — with an Undo right in the message. Or decide before you start: Swap day, under Replace / edit, trades today’s session with any other planned in the next seven days.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.15.001: Opening from the home screen now shows DOG FOOD and the mark on black while the app loads, instead of a blank screen. iPhone only picks this up when the app is added, so remove it from the home screen and add it again once to see it.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.18.001: Blocks have a purpose now, not only a position. A strength goal runs Muscle, then Strength, then Power — slow-fading strength first, explosive work last, with a jump or throw leading every lift day in the Power block. A muscle goal runs Muscle, Muscle, Strength. A running goal runs Base, Build, Sharpen: one quality run at most in Base, tempo leading in Build, intervals in Sharpen. Today shows which block you are in; Settings → Training Setup → This block lets you pick a different one for the current block and rebuilds the days ahead, with an Undo.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.18.002: Golf is in. Turn it on under Settings → Training Setup → Sports you play, pick your season and your round days. Round days become a Golf round on the calendar (G): a moving warm-up before you hit — no held stretches, they cost speed and accuracy — and stretches for after, aimed at the lead hip, upper back, lats and wrists. Every lift day gets one fast rotational movement (med-ball throws, woodchops, landmine rotations), the day before a round keeps heavy legs off it where the split allows, and the blocks run Strength then Power off-season, or two short, heavy lifts a week in-season.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.18.003: Lift days can end with a 6–8 minute finisher now — bike or rower intervals, an EMOM, a short AMRAP or carries, picked to spare whatever the day already worked. The time comes out of your session length, so a 60-minute day is still 60 minutes. None on a deload, after a power lead, the day before a golf round, or in sessions of 30 minutes or less, and you can switch them off in Training Setup. A new Engine block (Hyrox runs Strength then Engine; anyone can pick it) puts a finisher on every lift day and swaps one lift a week for a 20–24 minute metcon. Everything in them is low-skill on purpose: no cleans or deadlifts against a clock. Also fixed: Today halved the sets of a deload week that had already been halved when it was planned.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.18.004: Block length sets itself now, from what the block is for. Muscle and In-season blocks run 6 weeks, Strength and Base 5, Build and Engine 4, Power and Sharpen 3 — deload week included in each. Volume-building blocks run long, peaking blocks short because power fades within about a week, and nothing goes past six weeks without a deload (lifters deload about every 5½ weeks on average). Finished blocks keep the length they ran, so changing a goal or your golf season reshapes the block you are in and the ones ahead, never your history. A fixed length is still there under Training Setup → Block length if you want one.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.18.005: Switching to automatic block lengths no longer moves you. Blocks you had already finished keep the length they actually ran, so you stay in the same block and week you were in — only the block you are in now, and the ones after it, take their length from their type.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.18.006: Power blocks have more to work with. Pull days get an explosive pull to open with — Explosive Pull-up, Explosive Inverted Row, Pendlay Row or Kettlebell High Pull — where before they had none. Every Power-block day also adds a second fast movement for the other half of the body, a throw on leg days and a jump on upper days, alongside the heavy lift. And two days with the same pattern no longer open with the same jump: the second squat day gets the next one down. New for bodyweight training: the Incline Plyometric Push-up.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.20.001: New tab: Plan, between Today and Body. Three rows, one line each — which block you are in and what comes next, your goals, and your sport — and a tap on any of them opens the detail. Blocks shows the ones behind you and the next few ahead, and is where This block and Block length live now; Sport is where golf is set up. Both moved out of Settings, which keeps the things about you and the app.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.20.002: Icons. The week calendar shows each session as a shape instead of a letter — a bar for lifting, chevrons for a run, a quarter-circle for mobility, a stopwatch for a metcon, a flag for golf. Plan leads each row with one on a cut-corner tile, the block list marks each block (Muscle, Strength, Power and the rest have their own), and the Finisher, Metcon and Cool-down headings on Today carry theirs. One idea each, solid shapes, nothing drawn for its own sake.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.20.003: Weight guidance is in, on Plan under the block. It reads your weigh-ins against what the current block wants for your goal and sport — a slow gain in a Muscle block, steady to slightly up in Strength and golf off-season, steady in Power, the running blocks, in-season and deload weeks — and says in one line whether you are on target, below or above. Judged on the last three weeks, not on any single weigh-in. Tap it to log today’s weight. When you are off target, Today says so under the block line.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.22.015: The tab switcher under the masthead is five dots in a straight row now, and the tab you are on is a short white pill. Tap a dot or swipe as before.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.22.004: The mark is a flat white face now, with a soft shadow along the bottom so it still reads as round, and its eyes sit a little higher. Same on the app icon.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.22.003: The mark’s eyes are a third bigger and its outer ring is gone — a plain white face on the masthead and on the app icon.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.22.002: The mark is white with black eyes now, on every tab and on the app icon — one face across the app, with each tab’s colour left to its title. And the type is on one scale: every size in the app is one of nine steps (10, 11, 12, 13, 16, 18, 26, 46, 58), where there were fourteen, so labels, notes and numbers line up from screen to screen. Re-add the app to your home screen to pick up the new icon.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.22.001: Dogfood is now Touring. Same app, same colours, same mark — just cleaner: the + texture behind every panel is gone, buttons are lighter with hairline edges and a little more room to tap, and the section bands have more air around them. The launch screen shows the new name too; remove the app from your home screen and add it again once to pick up the new name and launch screen.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.21.003: Plan looks like the rest of the app now: numbered sections, the tag on the right saying where you are, one button to change each. Block shows this block’s weeks as a strip like Today’s calendar, deload hatched, with the blocks coming up under it. Goals lists each goal and whether it is moving. Sport shows each sport you play with its week — game days filled, training days as rings. Weight shows the number big, the trend against what the block wants, and what to do about it.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.21.002: Eleven more sports, alongside golf: soccer, basketball, tennis, cricket, rugby, AFL, volleyball, combat sports, cycling, swimming and climbing. Turn on as many as you play under Plan → Sport, with a season and two kinds of day for each. Game days (a match, a fight, a race) are kept for the game, with a warm-up before and stretches after, and heavy lifting stays off the day or two before. Training days share the day: a lift in the morning and your sport in the evening. Every lift day gets one fast movement and one protective one from each sport, picked from what the research says moves performance and injury risk for it: Nordics and Copenhagens for football codes, landing and tendon work for jumping sports, rotator-cuff work for throwing, serving and swimming, neck work for collision and fight sports, finger and antagonist work for climbing. Fifteen new exercises came in with them, and every sport has its own icon.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.21.001: Stalls and deloads act now, not just warn. A lift stuck at one weight for three sessions without reaching the top of its rep range resets about 10% and builds back; if it sticks again at the same weight, it tells you which variation to swap to. When two or more of your main lifts stop improving in the same block (none of the last three sessions beat the best before them, or the last two fall 3% short of it), the deload moves to next week and the block ends there, so you never get a second deload a fortnight later. Marking a deload yourself from week 3 does the same. This covers every main lift you train, goal or no goal. The weeks already planned after it are rebuilt for the new block, and one undo puts it all back.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.20.005: Hold a day on Today’s week strip. Drag it onto another day and it moves there — if that day has a session too, the two swap. Let go without moving and you get the day’s menu: move it, edit what is on it, add a session, clear it, or mark it as a day you are not training. Every change has an undo. Days that have passed, and days with a session already logged, stay where they are.
APP_NOTES.2026.10.20.004: Cuts are scheduled now, not just gains. When your body fat reads 20% or more (30% for women), or your weight has climbed 5% above its low of the last six months, the next Strength block becomes a cut: lose 0.4–0.6 kg a week for four weeks, with the deload as a week-long diet break at maintenance, then straight back to maintenance in the block after. Strength blocks are where a deficit costs least — strength keeps climbing, only muscle gain slows. Muscle blocks hold weight while a cut is due, and Power, the running sharpen blocks and golf in-season never cut. Plan’s block list shows what weight does in each block ahead.

APP_NOTES.2026.09.20.628: The header rule draws, a bar near its top says so, and a learned substitution swaps itself in.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.20.627: Five more motions — the pace writes itself, a deload drops from last week, the rest plate lifts.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.20.626: Four new motions in the log sheet — the over-plan plate lands, the separator key answers, the breakdown re-counts.
APP_NOTES.2026.09.20.625: The workout-streak counter goes, four years after the flame it fed left the masthead.

APP_NOTES.2026.09.17.619: No change you can see — two injury-rehab tables moved so the engine spec can read them.

meta_analysis.label: META-ANALYSIS
meta_analysis.note: Backed by a pooled analysis of many studies — the strongest evidence here. It grades how the evidence was gathered, not who it was gathered from: most exercise-comparison research is done in untrained people, who grow more and less specifically than trained ones.

systematic_review.label: REVIEW
systematic_review.note: Backed by a formal review of the published research. It grades how the evidence was gathered, not who it was gathered from: most exercise-comparison research is done in untrained people, who grow more and less specifically than trained ones.

rct.label: RCT
rct.note: Backed by a randomised controlled trial — one good study rather than many. Check who was in it: most exercise-comparison trials use untrained participants, who grow more and less specifically than trained ones.

coaching_consensus.label: CONSENSUS
coaching_consensus.note: What coaches broadly agree on, rather than a lab finding. Useful, just a different kind of evidence — and it comes from working with trained people, which the lab findings mostly do not.

strength.label: Strength — work toward a top set of ~5, or 5×5/3×5. Bigger jumps, lower reps.

hypertrophy.label: Hypertrophy — 3×8-12 or 4×8-10. Progress reps within range before adding weight.

power.label: Power — low reps, high intent, full rest between sets. Weight increases are small and infrequent — technical quality matters more than the number.

RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.easy: Walk, then run the first kilometre slower than target pace — that is the warm-up
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.recovery: Walk, then run the first kilometre slower than target pace — that is the warm-up
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.long: Easy jog to open up, starting slower than feels necessary — 5-10 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.tempo: Easy jog, last 2 minutes lifting toward steady — 10-15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.hills: Easy jog to the hill, then one relaxed uphill at half effort — 10-15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.sprint: Easy jog. Never sprint cold — 15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.race: Easy jog, finishing 25-30 min before the start — 10-15 min
RUN_RAISE_BY_TYPE.race_long: Easy jog to loosen off, finishing 15-20 min before the start — 5-10 min. The opening kilometres are the rest of the warm-up

RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.easy: Walk, then ease into the first kilometre slower than target pace. The run is the warm-up.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.long: 5-10 min easy jog to open up, then settle. Start slower than feels necessary.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.tempo: 10-15 min easy jog, last 2 min lifting toward steady · 4-6 × 80-100m strides · first rep within 2 min.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.interval: 10-15 min easy jog · 4-6 × 80-100m strides at target pace · rep one within 2 min.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.fartlek: 10 min easy jog · 3 × 20s strides. The first surge is the warm-up for the rest.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.hills: 10-15 min easy jog to the hill · one relaxed uphill at half effort before the working reps.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.sprint: 15 min easy jog · 4-6 progressive strides. Never sprint cold.
RUN_WARMUP_BY_TYPE.race: 10-15 min easy jog finishing 25-30 min out · 4-6 strides · keep moving with layers on, gap to the gun under 5 min. At half or full marathon distance cut the jog to 5-10 min and treat the first kilometres as the rest of it.

muscle.label: Muscle
muscle.note: Muscle block — 8–12 reps, volume building week to week.

strength.label: Strength
strength.note: Strength block — main lifts heavy at 3–6 reps; accessories stay 8–12.

power.label: Power
power.note: Power block — a jump or throw leads every lift day while you are fresh, main lifts stay heavy. Power fades within about a week of stopping, so it comes last.

base.label: Base
base.note: Base block — easy running volume, one quality run at most.

build.label: Build

combat.label: Combat sports
combat.seasonNote: Between fight camps the lifting builds muscle, then strength, then power, with a conditioning block last; once a fight is booked it drops to two short heavy sessions a week with nothing heavy in the two days before. If you're cutting weight, keep those sessions short and don't chase PRs.

TENDINOPATHY_PROTOCOL.high: Reactive/painful phase: isometric loading for immediate analgesic effect — wall sit or leg press hold (patellar) / heel-raise hold (Achilles), 5×30-45s at ~70% effort, daily.
TENDINOPATHY_PROTOCOL.mid: Progressive loading: heavy-slow-resistance (3-4s tempo up/down), 3x/week, 3-4 sets of 6-15 reps — or an eccentric heel-drop program, 3×15 reps, 2×/day. HSR and eccentric show comparable long-term efficacy; HSR is often better tolerated (less session pain).
TENDINOPATHY_PROTOCOL.low: Return to sport: plyometric and energy-storage loading (hopping, bounding) reintroduced progressively, criteria-based on pain ≤3/10 next-day — not purely time-based.
